data.def: Determines what information goes into the model and in which form, including the training corpus and tokenization strategy.
data.ex: ESM2 is trained on UniRef protein sequences tokenized as individual amino acids.
data.says: Data sets what can be known.
data.layer: Knowledge missing because observations were never or rarely collected.

arch.def: Determines how information is processed to extract and store learned properties, such as protein grammar.
arch.ex: The leading architecture, used by ESM2, is the Transformer, whose self-attention relates every token to every other token.
arch.says: Architecture sets which relationships can be captured efficiently.
arch.layer: Knowledge hard to learn because the architecture cannot span it.

train.def: Determines what the model is rewarded to learn.
train.ex: In masked language modeling, used by ESM2, randomly hidden amino acids are predicted from the surrounding sequence.
train.says: The training scheme sets what is rewarded and therefore what a model is good at.
train.layer: Knowledge hard to learn because the objective does not reward it, as with cause and effect.

evalu.def: Determines how the model is judged, at two levels: intrinsic and downstream.
evalu.ex: Intrinsic: whether ESM2 recovers residue contacts. Downstream: shared benchmarks such as ProteinGym.
evalu.layer: Capability hidden or exaggerated by evaluation.

post.def: Determines how a trained model is used: probing, fine-tuning, use as is, and interpretability analysis.
post.ex: ESM2 likelihoods score mutations with no further training; embeddings can be probed or fine-tuned.
post.layer: Knowledge present in the model but inaccessible to current analysis.

agent.layer: An agent that calls a foundation model inherits that model’s boundary, and adds an orchestration boundary of its own, since agents with the same tools can differ in how well they select and combine them.
